newsitem.title: USA: Ruling in Illinois incinerator bond case delayed.
newsitem.headline: Ruling in Illinois incinerator bond case delayed.

text.p: A ruling by a U.S. District Court judge in Chicago on whether or not to dismiss or delay a lawsuit challenging Illinois' removal of a state subsidy for a bond-financed waste-to-energy incinerator has been delayed.
The ruling scheduled for Wednesday by Judge Brian Duff was postponed until Oct. 23, according to attorneys representing the parties in the lawsuit.

Attorneys representing Illinois officials sued by the developer of an incinerator in the Chicago suburb of Robbins had asked the judge to dismiss the case on the grounds the 11th Amendment to the U.S. Constitution precludes lawsuits dealing with public funds.
In this case, public funds involved a subsidy Illinois had been guarenteeing to incinerator developers that allowed them to sell the electricity they generated to utilities at a higher rate.
If the lawsuit was not dismissed, the state asked the judge to defer the case until a similar lawsuit filed by other incinerator developers in Cook County Circuit Court was decided.

A decision on whether that case will be dismissed is expected within days. Following oral arguments earlier this month on the state's motion to dismiss the case, Judge Edwin Berman said he would rule by Monday.

At stake in both lawsuits is the viability of nearly $500 million of tax-exempt, unrated bonds that were sold for three incinerator projects in Robbins, Ford Heights and Fulton and which were largely dependent on the state subsidy.

CGE Ford Heights, the developer of the Ford Heights incinerator, has already filed for bankruptcy as its litigation against the state continues. That lawsuit has been joined by developer CGE Fulton and bondholders.

The Illinois Development Finance Authority sold $79.6 million of bonds for the Ford Heights project in 1994, while Fulton sold $84.6 million of bonds last December. The Fulton sale occured just before the Illinois General Assembly voted to yank the incinerator subsidy that had been in effect since 1987. The measure was signed into law in March by Gov. Jim Edgar.

Meanwhile, Foster Wheeler Corp. announced last week a tender offer for nearly $320 million of bonds sold by Robbins in 1994 for the incinerator had been initiated. Under the tender, which ends Oct. 15, the bonds would be restructured with a lower interest rate and additional credit support, as well as other changes.
The Robbins incinerator was developed by Illinois subsidiaries of Foster Wheeler.
